claim: Drosophila male germline stem cells (GSCs) attach to the hub, a major niche component that secretes the ligand, Unpaired (Upd).
source: Drosophila male germline stem cells (GSCs) attach to the hub, a major niche component that secretes the ligand, Unpaired (Upd).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work (Kiger et al., 2001; Tulina and Matunis, 2001) establishing this relationship.

claim: Upd binds to Domeless (Dome), a cytokine receptor homolog, leading to activation of the janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway to specify GSC identity.
source: Upd binds to Domeless (Dome), a cytokine receptor homolog, leading to activation of the janus kinase-signal transducer and activator of transcription (JAK-STAT) pathway to specify GSC identity (Kiger et al., 2001; Tulina and Matunis, 2001) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: GSCs divide asymmetrically by orienting their mitotic spindle perpendicular to the hub.
source: Within the context of this intercellular JAK-STAT self-renewal signaling, GSCs divide asymmetrically by orienting their mitotic spindle perpendicular to the hub (Yamashita et al., 2003; Yamashita et al., 2007) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and illustrated in Figure 1A.

claim: Spindle orientation is precisely prepared during interphase by stereotypical orientation of the mother and daughter centrosomes.
source: Spindle orientation is precisely prepared during interphase by stereotypical orientation of the mother and daughter centrosomes (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is illustrated in Figure 1A showing the positioning of centrosomes.

claim: Spindle orientation allows one daughter of the GSC division to remain attached to the hub to self-renew, while the other is displaced away from the hub to initiate differentiation.
source: This spindle orientation allows one daughter of the GSC division to remain attached to the hub to self-renew, while the other is displaced away from the hub to initiate differentiation.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge of asymmetric stem cell division and the role of spindle orientation.

claim: Upon knockdown of upd or dome, GSCs exhibited a dramatic increase in misoriented centrosomes and spindles.
source: Upon knockdown of upd or dome (upd-gal4, tub-gal80ts > UAS-updRNAi or nos-gal4ΔVP16, tub-gal80ts > UAS-domeRNAi after 4 days of RNAi induction), GSCs exhibited a dramatic increase in misoriented centrosomes and spindles (Figure 1D,G,I), indicating that Upd and Dome are critical for centrosome/spindle orientation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D, G, and I.

claim: Downregulation of JAK kinase (hopRNAi) or STAT transcription factor (stat92ERNAi, or temperature sensitive stat92Ets) barely affected either centrosome or spindle orientation.
source: Surprisingly, downregulation of JAK kinase (hopRNAi) or STAT transcription factor (stat92ERNAi, or temperature sensitive stat92Ets) barely affected either centrosome or spindle orientation (Figure 1E,H–I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1E, H, and I.

claim: upd and dome regulate GSC centrosome/spindle orientation independent of the transcriptional network regulated by the JAK kinase and STAT transcription factor.
source: These results indicate that upd and dome might regulate GSC centrosome/spindle orientation independent of the transcriptional network regulated by the JAK kinase and STAT transcription factor.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that hop and stat92E knockdown do not affect orientation despite affecting GSC maintenance.

claim: Introduction of hoptum-1 to domeRNAi genotype background significantly rescued the GSC loss phenotype.
source: Although domeRNAi (nos-gal4 > UAS-domeRNAi, without temporal control of RNAi) resulted in near complete loss of GSCs by the time of eclosion, introduction of hoptum-1 to this genotype background (hoptum-1, nos-gal4 > UAS-domeRNAi) significantly rescued the GSC loss phenotype ((9.1 ± 0.3 GSCs/testis in wild type control, 0.3 ± 0.1 GSCs/testis in domeRNAi, 4.9 ± 0.2 GSCs/testis in hoptum-1 domeRNAi, Figure 2A–C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data and images shown in Figure 2A-C.

claim: Despite that GSCs were well maintained in hoptum-1 domeRNAi, GSC centrosome/spindle were highly misoriented.
source: We found that, despite that GSCs were well maintained, GSC centrosome/spindle were highly misoriented (Figure 2D–F).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D-F.

claim: The centrosome/spindle orientation defect due to inactivation of upd or dome did not arise from the loss of GSC identity.
source: These results demonstrate that the centrosome/spindle orientation defect due to inactivation of upd or dome did not arise from the loss of GSC identity.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that GSCs with hoptum-1 domeRNAi maintain identity but have orientation defects.

claim: upd and dome regulate GSC centrosome/spindle orientation independent of the self-renewal pathway.
source: Taken together, we conclude that upd and dome regulate GSC centrosome/spindle orientation independent of the self-renewal pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the separation-of-function experiments showing orientation defects without loss of GSC identity.

claim: Dome localizes near the hub-GSC interface during interphase.
source: By using a specific anti-Dome antibody (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), we found that Dome localizes near the hub-GSC interface during interphase (Figure 3A), where centrosome is known to be anchored by microtubules (MTs) (Yamashita et al., 2007), implying that Dome might function in anchoring centrosomes to the hub-GSC interface.
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Dome localization at the hub-GSC interface was dependent on Upd.
source: Dome localization at the hub-GSC interface was dependent on Upd (Figure 3D,G), indicating that Upd might guide the localization of Dome.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3D and G.

claim: Expression of Upd from a single somatic cyst stem cell clone was sufficient to ectopically localize Dome in the neighboring GSCs.
source: Consistent with the idea that Upd directly guides Dome localization, expression of Upd from a single somatic cyst stem cell clone was sufficient to ectopically localize Dome in the neighboring GSCs (Figure 3I, n = 18 clones were examined).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3I.

claim: In mitosis, Dome translocated to the spindle, which was also dependent on Upd.
source: In mitosis, Dome translocated to the spindle (Figure 3B–C), which was also dependent on Upd (Figure 3E–F,H), again suggesting possible involvement of Dome in MT-dependent processes.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3B-C, E-F, and H.

claim: Dome localized to the mitotic spindle even in non-GSCs (i.e. gonialblasts (GBs) and spermatogonia (SGs)), but it was not dependent on Upd in these cells.
source: Interestingly, although Dome localized to the mitotic spindle even in non-GSCs (i.e. gonialblasts (GBs) and spermatogonia (SGs)), it was not dependent on Upd in these cells (Figure 3H), indicating that Upd regulates Dome's localization specifically in GSCs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3H.

claim: Dome localization was not affected in hopRNAi or stat92ERNAi.
source: Importantly, Dome localization was not affected in hopRNAi or stat92ERNAi (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), suggesting that only Upd, but not the JAK-STAT transcription network, is critical for Dome localization.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2.

claim: Dome colocalized with early endosomal marker Rab5 specifically in prophase.
source: Obvious colocalization was observed between Dome and early endosomal marker Rab5 specifically in prophase (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: Endogenous Rab5 was co-immunoprecipitated with Dome using Drosophila testes lysates enriched with GSCs, confirming their physical interaction.
source: Consistently, endogenous Rab5 was co-immunoprecipitated with Dome using Drosophila testes lysates enriched with GSCs, confirming their physical interaction (Figure 4D, nos-gal4 > UAS-dome-GFP, UAS-upd).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: A recycling endosome marker, Rab4, colocalized with Dome during prophase and physically interacted with Dome.
source: In addition, a recycling endosome marker, Rab4, colocalized with Dome during prophase and physically interacted with Dome (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A,F).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and F.

claim: Rab8 showed weak colocalization during prophase, but clear physical interaction between Rab8 and Dome was detected.
source: Rab8 showed weak colocalization during prophase, but clear physical interaction between Rab8 and Dome was detected (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C,H).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and H.

claim: A recycling endosome marker Rab11 showed colocalization with Dome at prophase, but physical interaction was barely detectable.
source: A recycling endosome marker Rab11 showed colocalization with Dome at prophase, but physical interaction was barely detectable (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D,I).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D and I.

claim: A late endosomal marker Rab7 and a recycling endosmal marker Rab35 showed no colocalization or physical interaction with Dome.
source: A late endosomal marker Rab7 and a recycling endosmal marker Rab35 showed no colocalization or physical interaction (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B,E,G).
evidence: This is supported by colocalization and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B, E, and G.

claim: Expression of dominant-negative forms of Rab4, 5, 8, and 11 perturbed localization of Dome and significantly increased centrosome/spindle misorientation.
source: These interactions between Dome and some endocytic components appear to be relevant, because expression of dominant-negative forms of Rab4, 5, 8, and 11 (nos-gal4 > UAS-YFP-rabDN) perturbed localization of Dome (Figure 4—figure supplement 2) and significantly increased centrosome/spindle misorientation (Figure 4E,F,G,I,J,L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2 and Figure 4E, F, G, I, J, and L.

claim: Expression of Rab7DN or Rab35DN showed little effect on centrosome/spindle orientation.
source: In contrast, expression of Rab7DN or Rab35DN showed little effect (Figure 4H,K,L).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4H, K, and L.

claim: Internalization of Dome via endocytosis, which allows its localization with the spindle pole/spindle in mitosis, is critical for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation.
source: These data suggest that internalization of Dome via endocytosis, which allows its localization with the spindle pole/spindle in mitosis, is critical for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that disrupting endocytic pathways affects Dome localization and centrosome/spindle orientation.

claim: Dome is reported to interact with Eb1, a major MT-binding protein.
source: By searching the Drosophila Interactions Database (www.droidb.org), we found that Dome is reported to interact with Eb1 (Guruharsha et al., 2011), a major MT-binding protein (Akhmanova and Steinmetz, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and database information.

claim: Endogenous Eb1 co-immunoprecipitated with Dome in Drosophila testes lysates enriched with GSCs.
source: We confirmed that endogenous Eb1 co-immunoprecipitated with Dome in Drosophila testes lysates enriched with GSCs (Figure 5A, nos-gal4 > UAS-dome-GFP, UAS-upd).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: RNAi-mediated knockdown of eb1 dramatically increased GSC centrosome/spindle misorientation.
source: RNAi-mediated knockdown of eb1 (nos-gal4 > UAS-eb1RNAi) dramatically increased GSC centrosome/spindle misorientation (Figure 5B–F), suggesting that Eb1 is involved in GSC centrosome/spindle orientation.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5B-F.

claim: Eb1 localization was dependent on dome specifically in GSCs, but not in GBs or SGs.
source: Interestingly, we found that Eb1 localization was dependent on dome specifically in GSCs, but not in GBs or SGs (Figure 5H,J,L,N,O,P), suggesting that the significance of Eb1-Dome interaction is specific to GSCs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5H, J, L, N, O, and P.

claim: Knockdown of eb1 resulted in compromised localization of Dome in GSCs but not in GBs/SGs.
source: Conversely, knockdown of eb1 (nos-gal4 > UAS-eb1RNAi) resulted in compromised localization of Dome in GSCs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–D,G,H), but not in GBs/SGs (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–F), again showing that Eb1/Dome's functional interdependence is likely specific to GSCs.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A-D, E-F, G, and H.

claim: Dome and Eb1 interact with each other in GSCs to regulate centrosome/spindle orientation.
source: Taken together, these results show that Dome and Eb1 interact with each other in GSCs to regulate centrosome/spindle orientation.
evidence: This is inferred from the mutual dependence of localization and the effects on centrosome/spindle orientation.

claim: Dome contains a SQIP sequence motif in its intracellular domain.
source: We found this motif (SQIP) in the intracellular domain of Dome (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: The SQIP sequence is essential for Dome-Eb1 interaction.
source: Indeed, we found that the SQIP sequence is essential for Dome-Eb1 interaction: Dome cytoplasmic fragment (with or without SQIP sequence) tagged with 6xHis was expressed in bacteria, purified with Ni-NTA agarose beads, and incubated with GSC extract expressing Eb1-GFP (see Materials and ethods). Whereas wild type Dome cytoplasmic fragment pulled down Eb1-GFP, Dome cytoplasmic fragment without SQIP did not (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is supported by pull-down assay data shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Dome cytoplasmic fragment is sufficient to interact with Eb1.
source: These results show that 1) Dome cytoplasmic fragment is sufficient to interact with Eb1, and 2) SQIP sequence is critical for interacting with Eb1.
evidence: This is inferred from the pull-down assay results.

claim: Both UAS-dome-GFP and UAS-dome∆SQIP-GFP were fully capable of activating the JAK-STAT pathway as evidenced by upregulation of STAT in GSCs.
source: Both UAS-dome-GFP and UAS-dome∆SQIP-GFP were fully capable of activating the JAK-STAT pathway as evidenced by upregulation of STAT in GSCs (Figure 6C–F), and supporting GSC self-renewal (Figure 6G).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6C-F and G.

claim: Despite its ability to effectively support GSC self-renewal, dome∆SQIP-GFP failed to orient centrosome/spindle.
source: Despite its ability to effectively support GSC self-renewal, dome∆SQIP-GFP failed to orient centrosome/spindle (Figure 6H–N), demonstrating that the interaction between Dome and Eb1 via SQIP sequence is critical for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation, independent of GSC self-renewal.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6H-N.

claim: The interaction between Dome and Eb1 via SQIP sequence is critical for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation, independent of GSC self-renewal.
source: Despite its ability to effectively support GSC self-renewal, dome∆SQIP-GFP failed to orient centrosome/spindle (Figure 6H–N), demonstrating that the interaction between Dome and Eb1 via SQIP sequence is critical for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation, independent of GSC self-renewal.
evidence: This is inferred from the separation-of-function mutation results.

claim: Dome's functions in self-renewal and centrosome/spindle orientation are separable.
source: Collectively, the data shown here argue that Dome orients GSC centrosomes/spindles via its interaction with Eb1. Also, the ability of dome∆SQIP-GFP to fully rescue GSC loss due to domeRNAi, while failing to rescue GSC centrosome/spindle orientation, further strengthens the notion that Dome's functions in self-renewal and centrosome/spindle orientation are separable (Figure 6O).
evidence: This is inferred from the separation-of-function mutation results and illustrated in Figure 6O.

claim: Dome localization was not affected in apc1 or apc2 mutants.
source: We found that Dome localization was not affected in apc1 or apc2 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 2A–F) or upon overexpression of dominant negative E-cadherin (Figure 6—figure supplement 2G–H).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2A-F and G-H.

claim: Localization of Eb1 was mostly unaffected in apc1 or apc2 mutants, except that Eb1 localization to the spindle was slightly compromised in apc2 mutants.
source: Conversely, localization of Eb1 was mostly unaffected under these conditions, except that Eb1 localization to the spindle was slightly compromised in apc2 mutants (Figure 6—figure supplement 2I–N).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2I-N.

claim: The localization of Apc1, Apc2 and E-cadherin was unaffected in updRNAi, domeRNAi and eb1RNAi testes.
source: Similarly, the localization of Apc1, Apc2 and E-cadherin was unaffected in updRNAi, domeRNAi and eb1RNAi testes (Figure 6—figure supplement 3A–I).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3A-I.

claim: The Upd-Dome-Eb1 and E-cad-Apc2/Apc1 axes appear to operate mostly separately.
source: Although we were not able to test whether these two axes function cooperatively to ensure centrosome/spindle orientation due to inability to combine all genotypes required (temporarily controlled domeRNAi and homozygosity of apc1 or apc2), above results suggest that the Upd-Dome-Eb1 and E-cad-Apc2/Apc1 axes appear to operate mostly separately (Figure 6—figure supplement 3J).
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of mutual dependence in localization and illustrated in Figure 6—figure supplement 3J.

claim: Many cytokine receptors contain SxI/LP motifs.
source: Indeed, we noticed that many cytokine receptors contain SxI/LP motifs, implying that their interaction with Eb1 may be widely conserved (Table 1).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Table 1.

claim: Gp130 contains SYLP sequence in its cytoplasmic domain.
source: Gp130, the mammalian cytokine receptor with the highest homology to Dome, contains SYLP sequence in its cytoplasmic domain (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Gp130 plays a critical role in the differentiation and development of T cells via activation of the JAK-STAT signaling.
source: Gp130 plays a critical role in the differentiation and development of T cells via activation of the JAK-STAT signaling (Silver and Hunter, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Immunological synapses formed between antigen-presenting cells and T-cells function as a signaling platform to facilitate T cell activation and proliferation.
source: Immunological synapses formed between antigen-presenting cells and T-cells function as a signaling platform to facilitate T cell activation and proliferation (Martín-Cófreces et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Naïve T-cells orient their centrosomes toward the immunological synapse, leading to oriented cell division with respect to the antigen-presenting cell.
source: It is well-established that naïve T-cells orient their centrosomes toward the immunological synapse, leading to oriented cell division with respect to the antigen-presenting cell (Chang et al., 2007; Oliaro et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Oriented division of naïve T-cells results in asymmetric division, generating memory and effector T cells.
source: This oriented division of naïve T-cells results in asymmetric division, generating memory and effector T cells (Arsenio et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Jurkat cells orient their centrosomes toward anti-CD3 coated beads upon binding.
source: We confirmed that Jurkat cells orient their centrosomes toward the beads upon binding and found that Gp130 was concentrated toward the bead (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: siRNA-mediated knockdown of Gp130 dramatically reduced centrosome orientation toward the bead.
source: Strikingly, siRNA-mediated knockdown of Gp130 dramatically reduced centrosome orientation toward the bead (Figure 7C–D), suggesting that Gp130 is required for correct centrosome orientation at the immunological synapse.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7C-D.

claim: Gp130 is required for correct centrosome orientation at the immunological synapse.
source: Strikingly, siRNA-mediated knockdown of Gp130 dramatically reduced centrosome orientation toward the bead (Figure 7C–D), suggesting that Gp130 is required for correct centrosome orientation at the immunological synapse.
evidence: This is inferred from the siRNA knockdown results.

claim: Gp130 binds Eb1 in an SYLP-dependent manner.
source: Further extending the parallel between Dome and Gp130, we found that Gp130 binds Eb1 in an SYLP-dependent manner (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 7E.

claim: The SYLP sequence is essential for centrosome orientation toward the anti-CD3-coated bead.
source: Moreover, the SYLP sequence is essential for centrosome orientation toward the anti-CD3-coated bead, because Gp130 lacking SYLP failed to rescue centrosome misorientation caused by siRNA-mediated knockdown of Gp130 (Figure 7F–H, note that rescue constructs are designed to be insensitive to siRNA).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 7F-H.

claim: Eb1-binding to the cytoplasmic domain of a cytokine receptor is an evolutionarily conserved mechanism to orient the centrosomes in order to direct subsequent asymmetric cell divisions.
source: These data suggest that Eb1-binding to the cytoplasmic domain of a cytokine receptor is an evolutionarily conserved mechanism to orient the centrosomes in order to direct subsequent asymmetric cell divisions.
evidence: This is inferred from the parallel findings in Drosophila GSCs and mammalian T cells.

claim: The receptor Dome plays dual roles in activating the JAK-STAT pathway for GSC self-renewal and orienting the GSC spindle to allow asymmetric stem cell division.
source: Here, we show that the receptor Dome plays dual roles in activating the JAK-STAT pathway for GSC self-renewal and orienting the GSC spindle to allow asymmetric stem cell division.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results showing separation of these two functions.

claim: These two functions of Dome are entirely separable.
source: We show that these two functions are entirely separable and the spindle orientation is mediated by Dome's direct interaction with the microtubule regulator Eb1.
evidence: This is based on the separation-of-function mutation results.

claim: Spindle orientation is mediated by Dome's direct interaction with the microtubule regulator Eb1.
source: We show that these two functions are entirely separable and the spindle orientation is mediated by Dome's direct interaction with the microtubule regulator Eb1.
evidence: This is based on the biochemical and genetic interaction data.

claim: Cytokine receptor-Eb1 interaction is evolutionarily conserved.
source: Finally, we show that cytokine receptor-Eb1 interaction is evolutionarily conserved, with a mammalian cytokine receptor, Gp130, regulating the centrosome orientation toward a model immunological synapse.
evidence: This is based on the parallel findings in Drosophila and mammalian systems.

claim: Integration of two functions (cell polarity and fate) in a single receptor is a key mechanism to ensure an asymmetric outcome following cell division.
source: Taken together, we propose a novel mechanism by which a single receptor couples cell polarity with cell fate to ensure obligatory asymmetric division.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: The niche ligand may provide a spatial cue to the stem cell receptor, which in turn directly regulates MTs to orient the stem cell centrosomes/spindles.
source: We propose that the niche ligand may provide a spatial cue to the stem cell receptor, which in turn directly regulates MTs to orient the stem cell centrosomes/spindles.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: By being responsible for both cell fate determination and orientation, the single receptor species obligatorily combines these two processes.
source: Integrating activation of signaling pathway and spindle orientation into a single ligand-receptor combination has an important implication: by being responsible for both cell fate determination and orientation, the single receptor species obligatorily combines these two processes.
evidence: This is a speculative proposal based on the experimental findings.

claim: Endocytosis of the receptor Dome is critical for spindle orientation.
source: First, we showed that endocytosis of the receptor Dome is critical for spindle orientation.
evidence: This is based on the experimental results with Rab GTPases.

claim: Dome and several endocytic Rab GTPases colocalized at the spindle pole during prophase, and these Rab GTPases were required for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation.
source: Dome and several endocytic Rab GTPases colocalized at the spindle pole during prophase, and these Rab GTPases were required for GSC centrosome/spindle orientation.
evidence: This is based on the colocalization and functional studies with Rab GTPases.

claim: When Dome localizes to the spindle during metaphase, it is not colocalized with any endocytic Rab GTPases examined.
source: Curiously, when Dome localizes to the spindle during metaphase, it is not colocalized with any endocytic Rab GTPases examined (Figure 4C), implying that Dome might not be associated with the membrane compartment any longer.
evidence: This is based on the colocalization data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Dome might be cleaved to release the intracellular domain during metaphase.
source: If so, it indicates that Dome is cleaved to release the intracellular domain, which contains Eb1-binding sequence (and the antigen sequence against which Dome antibody was raised).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the observation that Dome is not associated with membrane compartments during metaphase.

claim: Defects in Upd-Dome-Eb1 axis result in misorientation of both centrosomes in interphase and spindles in mitosis.
source: Second, as mentioned above, defects in Upd-Dome-Eb1 axis result in misorientation of both centrosomes in interphase and spindles in mitosis, indicating that this axis is involved not only in centrosome orientation but also in the centrosome orientation checkpoint (COC).
evidence: This is based on the experimental results showing both centrosome and spindle misorientation.

claim: Upd-Dome-Eb1 axis is involved not only in centrosome orientation but also in the centrosome orientation checkpoint (COC).
source: Second, as mentioned above, defects in Upd-Dome-Eb1 axis result in misorientation of both centrosomes in interphase and spindles in mitosis, indicating that this axis is involved not only in centrosome orientation but also in the centrosome orientation checkpoint (COC).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both centrosome and spindle misorientation occur.

claim: Upd-Dome might contribute to dictating the location where the centrosome must be positioned, lack of which leading to defective sensing of misoriented centrosomes.
source: Based on the results presented in this study and considering the fact that Upd-Dome interaction would provide an ideal spatial cue for correct centrosome positioning, we speculate that Upd-Dome might contribute to dictating the location where the centrosome must be positioned, lack of which leading to defective sensing of misoriented centrosomes (i.e. defective COC activity).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the experimental findings.

claim: Upd and/or Dome might regulate certain aspects of Baz, which in turn regulate the COC activity.
source: In our previous study, we showed that a polarity protein Bazooka forms the 'docking site' at the hub-GSC interface, to which the centrosome has to associate to satisfy the COC (Inaba et al., 2015b). It is tempting to speculate that Upd and/or Dome might regulate certain aspects of Baz, which in turn regulate the COC activity.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on prior work and current findings.

claim: Knockdown of Dome or Eb1 did not result in spindle defects in general, as evidenced by the lack of obvious phenotypes in non-GSC germ cells.
source: Knockdown of Dome or Eb1 did not result in spindle defects in general, as evidenced by the lack of obvious phenotypes in non-GSC germ cells (GBs/SGs).
evidence: This is based on the observation that non-GSC germ cells do not show spindle defects.

claim: Inter-dependence of localization to the spindle between Dome and Eb1 was observed only in GSCs.
source: Moreover, inter-dependence of localization to the spindle between Dome and Eb1 was observed only in GSCs.
evidence: This is based on the localization studies in GSCs versus non-GSC germ cells.

claim: Dome-Eb1 interaction is only relevant in GSCs.
source: These results indicate that Dome-Eb1 interaction is only relevant in GSCs.
evidence: This is inferred from the GSC-specific effects of Dome and Eb1 knockdown.

claim: GSCs might have distinct microtubule characteristics, for example dynamics and/or asymmetry.
source: One explanation for the GSC-specific requirement of Dome-Eb1 interaction is that GSCs might have distinct microtubule characteristics, for example dynamics and/or asymmetry.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain the GSC-specific requirement.

claim: Dome might modulate microtubule characteristics by recruiting Eb1 to the microtubule.
source: Dome might modulate microtubule characteristics by recruiting Eb1 to the microtubule.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the interaction between Dome and Eb1.

claim: GSC-specific microtubule characteristics might necessitate Dome's aid for Eb1 to function properly.
source: Although Eb1 can bind to and regulate microtubule behavior on its own, GSC-specific microtubule characteristics might necessitate Dome's aid for Eb1 to function properly.
evidence: This is speculative reasoning to explain the GSC-specific requirement.

claim: This mechanism may be widely utilized by signaling cells to ensure asymmetric cell division of their target cells.
source: Our study further revealed a striking conservation of the cytokine receptor-Eb1 axis to orient the centrosomes in diverse systems: as distant as the Drosophila male GSCs and mammalian (model) immunological synapse. This mechanism may be widely utilized by signaling cells (e.g. niche cells and antigen-presenting cells) to ensure asymmetric cell division of their target cells (e.g. stem cells and T cells).
evidence: This is speculative reasoning based on the conservation observed in two systems.

claim: A single receptor regulates cell fate and cell polarity, thereby coordinating two critical aspects of asymmetric cell division.
source: In summary, our study demonstrates that a single receptor regulates cell fate and cell polarity, thereby coordinating two critical aspects of asymmetric cell division.
evidence: This is the main conclusion based on all the experimental findings.
